notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward.
Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Vincent Trocheck and Logan Cooley.
Jonathan Marchessault returned in their last game after missing 7 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Nicolas Hague returned in their last game after missing 8 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for fifth in the Central with 25 points, 2 points behind the Predators, fourth. A regulation win for the Mammoth would pull them level with the Predators.

NSH.head: The Predators have a hill to climb
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators can pull it off if their power play gets going.

UTA.head: The Mammoth should have the upper hand
UTA.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Kerfoot meets his old team
paras: The Mammoth (11-9-3) beat Colorado 4-1 on Nov 18, while the Predators (11-6-5) lost 7-3 to Minnesota on Nov 17. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth fifth (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Preds fourth (tied for 12th).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.543) says: their chances are worth about .706, and their goaltending has held them back. The Predators’ record (.614) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.530), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (3rd). As for the Predators, they keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd). They also get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st), so the Mammoth’s forecheck could keep them pinned in their own end. The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven goals in eleven games against Nashville since 2023-24. Logan Cooley (11 G / 12 A / 23 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Predators, Filip Forsberg (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Steven Stamkos (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Karel Vejmelka (6-7-2 / .869 SV% in 15 GS) has struggled for Utah so far, but will likely start. Juuse Saros (7-4-4 / .918 SV% in 15 GS) has been outstanding for Nashville and will likely start.

At home, Andrew Brunette likes to send Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against O'Brien, Stenlund and But. Elsewhere, the Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.

items.text: Alexander Kerfoot faces Utah for the first time since leaving.

The Mammoth have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Wild are missing more right now.
Mavrik Bourque has no goals on chances worth about 3.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Steven Stamkos has a point in four straight games.
